However, due to a recession in the market the following year, the investment fell by a percentage equal to one-fifth of the growth rate in the first year. After two years, his investment was ₹6750. Find the percentage of loss in the second year if it is known that the value of his investment never exceeded ₹10000 during the two years.
questions.solution_text:
Let percentage of growth in first year be $5x\%$
So percentage of loss in second year will be $x\%$
So, $5000\left(1+\dfrac{5x}{100}\right)\left(1-\dfrac{x}{100}\right)=6750$
or, $\left(1+\dfrac{5x}{100}\right)\left(1-\dfrac{x}{100}\right)=\dfrac{6750}{5000}=1.35$ ----->(1)
Let $\dfrac{x}{100}=k$
So, from equation (1),
$\left(1+5k\right)\left(1-k\right)=1.35$
or, $4k-5k^2=0.35$
or, $100k^2-80k+7=0$
or, $\left(10k-1\right)\left(10k-7\right)=0$
or, $k=\dfrac{1}{10}$ or $\dfrac{7}{10}$
or, $x=10$ or $70$
But, $x=70$ is rejected because in that case, after the first year the investment will become $5000\left(1+5\times\ \frac{70}{100}\right)=22500$ which is greater than $10000$
So, $x=10$
so, percentage loss in second year is $10\ \%\ \ $

questions.question_text: There are six numbers - a,b,c,d,e,f - such that their average is 11. The average of a,b, and c is e, the average of d and e is b, and the average of e and f is c. Find the value of e, if the value of a is 3.
questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{a+b+c}{3}=e$ => $a+b+c=3e$ => $b+c=3e-a\rightarrow1$
Also, $\dfrac{d+e}{2}=b$ => $d+e=2b\rightarrow2$
And, $\dfrac{e+f}{2}=c$ => $e+f=2c\rightarrow3$
Adding eq. 2 and eq. 3 -
=> $d+2e+f=2(b+c)$        (substituting the value of (b+c) from eq. 1)
=> $d+2e+f=6e-2a$
=> $d+f=4e-2a\rightarrow4$
Now, the average of all 6 numbers is 11.
=> $\dfrac{a+b+c+d+e+f}{6}=11$
=> $(a+e)+(b+c)+(d+f)=66$     (substituting the value of (b+c) and (d+f) from eq. 1 and eq. 4)
=> $(a+e)+(3e-a)+(4e-2a)=66$        
=> $8e-2a=66$        (And we are given the value of a = 3)
=> $8e=72$ => $e=9$

questions.question_text: If a 3-digit number is picked whose sum of the digits is 9, what is the probability that the number has either 1 or 2 or both?
questions.solution_text:
The number of three-digit numbers with the sum of the digits as 9 can be calculated as,
Let the three-digit number be xyz and we know that x + y + z = 9 and $x\ \ge\ 1\ ,\ \ y\ge\ 0\ ,\ z\ge\ 0$
Let a = x + 1, and the equation becomes,
a + y + z = 8
Number of possibilities = $^{8\ +\ 3\ -1}C_{3\ -\ 1}\ =\ ^{10}C_2\ =\ 45$ 
The numbers with 1 or 2 in it are,
8, 1, 0 - 4 numbers
7, 2, 0 - 4 numbers
7, 1, 1 - 3 numbers
6, 2, 1 - 6 numbers
5, 3, 1 - 6 numbers
5, 2, 2 - 3 numbers
4, 4, 1 - 3 numbers
4, 3, 2 - 6 numbers
Total = 4 + 4 + 3 + 6 + 6 + 3 + 3 + 6 = 35 ways.
Probability of the number containing either 1 or 2 or both = $\dfrac{35}{45}\ =\ \dfrac{7}{9}$
Hence, the correct answer is option B.

questions.question_text: Find the number of integral values of $p$ such that the equation $x^2-\left(p+2\right)x+\left(2p+9\right)=0$ has negative real roots.
questions.solution_text:
The equation given is, $x^2-\left(p+2\right)x+\left(2p+9\right)=0$
The conditions we need to check for two negative roots will be, we already notice the coefficient of the $x^2$ term is positive, so taking that into account, we have: 
1. $D\ge0$
2. The sum of the roots is negative 
3. Product of roots is positive
1.  $D\ge0$: 
$\left(p+2\right)^2-4\left(2p+9\right)\ge0$
$\left(p^2+4+4p\right)-4\left(2p+9\right)\ge0$
$p^2-4p-32\ge0$
$\left(p+4\right)\left(p-8\right)\ge0$
So we have either, $p\le-4\ or\ p\ge8$
2. $p+2<0$
We get: $p<-2$
So, the earlier case of $p>8$ is eliminated. 
3. $2p+9>0$
We get: $p>-4.5$
The final condition is, $p\in\ \left(-4.5,\ -4\right]$
The only value that satisfies this condition is p=-4.

questions.question_text: A man has 100 kg of grains of 2 types, A and B, in a ratio of 2:3. Grain A sells for Rs.10 less per kg than Grain B. Sita and Gita each purchase some amount of Grain A and B, and at the end, Sita pays Rs 200 more than Gita. If it is known that no grain is left with the man, and Gita buys 20kg of grain B, how many kg of grain A did Sita buy?
questions.solution_text:
We are given that the man has 2 types of grain in 2:3 ratio, and the total grain with the man is 100 kgs.
$\therefore$  quantity of grain A= $\dfrac{\ 2}{\left(2+3\right)}\times\ 100=\ \dfrac{\ 2}{5}\times\ 100=40\ kgs$
and quantity of grainB= $100-40=60kgs$
let Cost per kg of grain A be Rs k, then Cost per kg of grain B will be Rs (k+10)
Further, lets assume that Sita buys $\ x\ kg$ of grain A, and $\ y\ kg$ of grain B
while Gita buys $\ m\ kg$ of grain A and $\ n\ kg$ of grain B . 
$\ \therefore\ \ x+m=40\ ......\left(1\right)\ $
$\&\ \ y+n=60\ ......\left(2\right)\ $
Given , Gita buys $20\ kg\ $ of grain B , $i.e\ n=20\ $
$\therefore\ y=60-20=\ 40\ \ \ \left(eqn\ 2\right)$
Now, Sita pays Rs 200 more than Gita.
Amount paid by Sita= $x\times\ k\ +y\times\ \left(k+10\right)$
Amount paid by Gita= $m\times\ k\ +n\times\ \left(k+10\right)$
$\therefore\ x\times\ k\ +\ y\times\ \left(k+10\right)-\left\{m\times\ k\ +n\times\ \left(k+10\right)\right\}=200$
$or,\ \left(x+y-m-n\right).k\ +10.\left(y-n\right)=200$
$or,\ \ \left(x-m+40-20\right).k+10.\left(40-20\right)=200$
$or,\ \ \left(x-m+20\right).k+200=200$
$or,\ \ \left(x-m+20\right).k=0$
Now , k= cost per Kg cannot be 0, hence $x-m+20=0\ $
$or,\ x-m=-20\ .....\left(3\right)$
Solving Eqn 1 and 3, 
$x=10\ kg$
Hence, Amount of grain Sita bought=$10\ kg$

Equations 1 and 2 can be seen as linear equations in two variables.
Upon solving them, we get 
f(18) = $-\frac{4}{3}$, f(8) = $\frac{56}{3}$
2f(18)+5f(8) = $-\frac{8}{3}+\frac{280}{3}\ =\ \frac{272}{3}=90.67$

questions.question_text: Ashim sold 150 kgs of alphonso mangoes by marking up the price by 20% and offered free totapuri mangoes with every purchase. The price of Alphonso mangoes is 2.5 times the price of Totapuri mangoes. If it is known that he made a profit of $\dfrac{100}{11}\%$, how many kgs of totapuri mangoes did he give out for free to purchasers ?
questions.solution_text:
Let, price of Totapuri mangoes be Rs. x per kg.
Then, price of Alphonso mangoes is Rs. 2.5x per kg
Let us assume that he offers k kgs of Totapuri mangoes for every 1 kg of alphonso sold.
Then, effective cost price for 1 kg alphonso becomes 2.5x+kx =Rs (2.5+k)x
Ashim sells the Alphonso by marking up the price by 20%. 
So, selling price of 1kg  Alphonso mangoes is= $\left(1+20\%\right)\times\ 2.5\ x=Rs.\ 3x$ 
His profit percent is given to be $\dfrac{100}{11}\ \%\ $
So, $\dfrac{3x-\left(2.5+k\right)x}{\left(2.5+k\right)x}\times\ 100=\dfrac{100}{11}$
or, $\dfrac{0.5-k}{2.5+k}=\dfrac{1}{11}$
or, $11\left(0.5-k\right)=2.5+k$
or, $k=\dfrac{1}{4}kg\ $
So Ashim gives away $\dfrac{1}{4}kg\ $ of Totapuri for every 1 kg alphonso sold. Since as he sold 150 kg of Alphonso , so he should have given out $\dfrac{150}{4}=37.5\ kg$ of totapuri mangoes. 
Alternate Explanation,
Let cost price of totapuri mangoes be ₹1/kg
So, cost price of Alphonso mangoes will be ₹2.5/kg
So, marked price of Alphonso mangoes = ₹(2.5*1.2)/kg=₹3/kg

While returning, he travels 2T hours each by train and on foot, then covers the rest by bus.

Thus, the total time while returning from the office = $2T+2T+\dfrac{100-50T}{30}\rightarrow2$
Since the time taken in both journeys is equal, we will equate eq. 1 and 2 -
=> $20-8T=4T+\dfrac{100-50T}{30}$
=> $20-12T=\dfrac{100-50T}{30}$

Due to high tide, the stream's speed increases by two times its original speed on a particular day. On that day, the same boat travels from port A to port B and returns. What will the percentage increase/decrease be in the total journey time of the boat, assuming it travels with the same speed on both days?

Let original speed of boat be $b$ km/h and speed of stream be $s$ km/h
Also, let distance from port A to port B be $D$ km
Now, in the first case,
$\dfrac{D}{b+s}=2$ and $\dfrac{D}{b-s}=3$
or, $b+s=\dfrac{D}{2}$
$b-s=\dfrac{D}{3}$
Upon solving, 
$b=\dfrac{5D}{12}$ and $s=\dfrac{D}{12}$
Now, in the second case,
Speed of stream increases by 2 times the original speed
So, new speed of stream is $3s$
or, new speed of stream is $3\times\ \dfrac{D}{12}=\dfrac{D}{4}$
So, time required for downstream journey = $\dfrac{D}{b+3s}=\dfrac{D}{\dfrac{5D}{12}+\dfrac{D}{4}}=1.5$ hours
time required for upstream journey = $\dfrac{D}{b-3s}=\dfrac{D}{\dfrac{5D}{12}-\dfrac{D}{4}}=6$ hours
So, total time required = $1.5+6=7.5$ hours
Original time was $2+3=5$ hours
So, percentage increase = $\dfrac{7.5-5}{5}\times\ 100=50\ \%\ $

questions.question_text: 10 inlet pipes fill the tank in 4 hours, and n outlet pipes empty half the tank in 3 hours. If (n+1) inlet pipes and $\dfrac{n}{2}$ outlet pipes are opened, then the tank is filled in 24 hours. Find the ratio of the efficiency of the inlet to the outlet pipes.
questions.solution_text:
Let the efficiency of inlet pipes be a, and the outlet pipes be b.
10 inlet pipes fill the tank in 4 hours, thus the capacity of the tank will be = $10\times4\times a=40a$ litres
n outlet pipe empties half the tank in 3 hours; thus, the capacity of half the tank = $n\times3\times b=3nb$ litres. Thus, the capacity of the full tank is = $6nb$ litres.
=> $40a=6nb$ => $a=\dfrac{3nb}{20}\rightarrow1$
Now, (n+1) inlet pipes and $\dfrac{n}{2}$ outlet pipes are opened, and the tank is filled in 24 hours.
=> $\left(\left(n+1\right)a-\left(\dfrac{n}{2}\right)b\right)\times24=6nb$     (substituting the value of a from eq. 1)
=> $\left(\left(n+1\right)\left(\dfrac{3nb}{20}\right)-\left(\dfrac{n}{2}\right)b\right)=\dfrac{nb}{4}$
Cancelling the terms n and b from both LHS and RHS -
=> $\left(n+1\right)\dfrac{3}{20}-\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{1}{4}$
=> $\left(n+1\right)\dfrac{3}{20}=\dfrac{3}{4}$
=> $n+1=5$ => $n=4$
Substituting the value of n in eq. 1 -
$a=\dfrac{3\times4\times b}{20}$
=> $\dfrac{a}{b}=\dfrac{3}{5}$

Let the volume of the tank be $1$ litre, and it takes 10 * 4 = 40 hours for the inlet pipe to fill the tank. Thus - 
Efficiency of one inlet pipe = $\dfrac{1}{40}$ litre/hr

Now, we notice the dividend: $\left(5x^2+16x-10\right)^{^2}-\left(x^2+14x-8\right)^{^2}$

questions.question_text: A large sphere of radius R cm is melted to form N smaller spheres of radius r cm. The large sphere is painted blue at Rs. 36/cm², and each smaller sphere is painted red at Rs. 1/cm². If the total painting cost remains the same for both cases, find the value of N.

A large sphere of radius R cm is melted to form N smaller spheres of radius r cm.
=> $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3=N\times\ \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$
$=>R=N^{\frac{1}{3}}\times\ r$
Now, the large sphere is painted blue at Rs. 36/cm². 
=> Cost of painting the large sphere = $36\times\ 4\pi R^2$
And each smaller sphere is painted red at Rs. 1/cm²
=> Cost of painting all smaller spheres = $N\times\ 1\times\ 4\pi r^2$
The total painting cost remains the same for both cases.
=> $36\times\ 4\pi R^2=N\times\ 1\times\ 4\pi r^2$
Eliminating $4\pi$ both sides and then taking root-
=> $6\times\ R=N^{\frac{1}{2}}\times r$
Substituting the value of R from 1
$6\times N^{\frac{1}{3}}\times\ r=N^{\frac{1}{2}}\times r$
=> $6=N^{\frac{1}{6}}$
=> $N=6^6=46656$

So his efficiency y in the second case should be $\dfrac{112}{89.6\ }=1.25\ $ units per day.
